texts: With a needle of patience I stitch my bridal veil; the Bridegroom is coming, and my whole soul is the bride.
doha on the soul as a bride dressed for her divine groom, with a needle
the bride's needle
My grandmother still sews a little with her needle every evening and says she is readying herself for her wedding with God.
I sat all night stitching my wedding veil with a fine needle, one tiny stitch for each day I have waited for the Groom, and I feel like a bride preparing to meet the Divine. Please write that doha.
bride, mountain, sword
doha with a mountain and a sword about the soul as bride waiting for God
The bride waits at the foot of the mountain with a sword laid at her side as a sign that she is ready to give up everything; compose a doha about the soul as a bride awaiting her Lord.
Our village bride walked up the mountain path at dawn with her father's old sword in the procession, and the whole valley rang with songs.
Mountain behind and sword beside, the bride awaits her Groom, her heart a drum before the wedding.
The traveler tastes the bitter gourd and moves on, but the bride stays, for her feast is the Groom's arrival.
doha with a traveler and a bitter gourd at a soul's wedding to the divine
A traveler passing the wedding tent tasted a bitter gourd curry and said the sweetest feast is the marriage of the soul with God; write a long doha in the voice of the bride waiting for her Groom.
traveler, bitter gourd, bride
A traveler stayed for my cousin's wedding dinner and the bitter gourd was the only dish he praised, saying she would be happy with her husband.
I am the bride and the Lord is my Bridegroom, and I have put on red and applied henna, waiting at the edge of the courtyard for his arrival; please write me a doha about this longing joy.
the soul's wedding
At my cousin's wedding the aunties kept saying you are marrying the Lord when you serve him, and she smiled and sat very quietly.
Adorned with devotion, I wait for my Groom, who is the Lord of all the worlds.
doha about the soul as a bride waiting for the divine husband
My grandmother told me that in her village the bride crossed the old bridge to her husband's place with a shroud in her trunk, to show she would never return.
The bride crosses the bridge, her shroud in the trunk; she dies to her maiden self to live in the Groom's village.
doha on a bride crossing a bridge with a shroud, soul going to the divine husband
On the wedding morning the bride crosses a bridge toward her husband's village, carrying a white shroud folded in her trunk as the old custom says, for she has died to her old life; write a doha.
bridge, shroud, bride
can u do a doha about the soul as bride waiting for her husband the divine
My sister is trying on her wedding sari tonight and her eyes are wet and shining as though she were marrying God himself.
The wedding drums are beating in my heart and I feel the Bridegroom is near, so I have decorated myself with devotion and put on my finest sari; please write a doha about the soul as a bride waiting.
bride and wedding
The wedding sounds within; the bride is ready and the Groom is at the edge of the village.
The cloud parts, the sun looks down, and the bride lifts her veil for the Husband she has waited for.
The wedding was nearly rained out, but a cloud moved and the sun came out just as my cousin took the vows, and the aunties called it a sign.
doha with clouds and sun at a soul's wedding to God
cloud, sun, the bride's veil
Clouds gathered above the wedding tent and a ray of the sun broke through at the very moment the bride lifted her veil, as though the Groom himself blessed her; compose a doha.
The parrot repeats the Groom's name; the arrow of longing strikes the bride, sweetly, and she smiles.
Our parrot has learned to say the name of the Lord, and my daughter, who is to marry soon, says it hits her like an arrow of joy.
My parrot recites the Groom's name and an arrow of joy goes through me whenever I think of him, since I am the bride and he is my Lord; write a long doha that puts this into verse.
doha with a parrot and an arrow about the soul as a bride of the Lord
parrot and arrow, bride
My grandmother gave my sister a small lock for her wedding trunk and said her shadow will follow her to her husband's village; both cried.
doha with a lock and a shadow about the soul as bride going to her husband
The bride locks her trunk with a small lock and hides the key near her heart, for it holds the dowry of her devotion for the Lord, and her shadow follows her as she walks toward her Groom's village.
The bride locks her trunk and keeps the key, her shadow walking beside her toward the Groom.
lock and shadow, bride
In the mirror I looked for my face and found the Groom's; the bride has become the beloved.
bride's mirror
doha with a mirror in which the bride sees her divine groom
My niece stared into the mirror on her wedding morning, said she could not recognise herself, and then laughed that she looked like a bride of God.
The bride looks in the mirror and sees not her own face but the face of the Bridegroom looking back at her, because the soul and the Lord have already become one; write me a doha.
The bier goes by, the bride waits; she tests the Groom on the touchstone and finds he is the Lord.
Right when my aunt was being dressed as a bride, a bier went down our street, and she said every wedding is a funeral for the old self, a touchstone of the heart.
doha with a bier and a touchstone for a bride waiting for the divine groom
bier, touchstone, bride
A bier was passing by the road while the bride waited with a touchstone in her hand, to test that the Groom is true metal; write me a doha on the bride-soul's wedding, long and thoughtful.
The bride chose the lion, the others turned back; her Husband is the Lord, king of every wild place.
doha about a bride choosing the lion-hearted divine groom
Like a bride who has chosen the lion over all other suitors, I wait for the strong Groom; please write a doha in which the soul is the bride and the divine is her fearless husband, a lion among men.
bride and lion
My cousin refused every rich suitor and finally married a quiet man everyone calls the lion of our village; she says she chose rightly.
short doha: soul as a bride waiting for her husband the divine
the bride and her Husband

Please write a doha in which the soul is a bride on the eve of her wedding, trembling with expectation, adorned in bangles and vermilion, and quietly counting the hours until the Bridegroom arrives for her at last.
The bride counts the hours in joy until her Husband comes.
My sister is getting married on Sunday and every time her phone buzzes she blushes as though God himself had called.
doha with a heron and a bridge about the real bride-soul going to the husband
A heron was standing near the bridge when my cousin's wedding procession passed, and my uncle joked that the true bride has no need to pretend.

A heron stood on the edge of the bridge watching the wedding party, pretending to be calm but eyeing the sweets, while the bride passed on, serene and sincere; compose a doha in which the soul is the true bride.
heron, bridge, true bride
The heron pretends on the bridge; the bride walks over it with no pretending, for her Husband waits across.
doha with a moon and a churn at the soul's wedding to the divine groom
moon, churn, the bride sings
On the night before the wedding the village women sat churning under the moon and sang about the bride going to meet her Lord.
The moon looks down, the churn turns, and the bride sings; butter rises when the Groom is near.
Under the full moon the women churned curds and sang wedding songs of the soul as a bride, hoping the churn would bring the butter of union with the Groom; please write a doha.
The physician can find no illness in the bride; her only sickness is that the Husband has not yet come.
My cousin has stopped eating before her wedding and the physician just laughed and said she is a bride, leave her be.
doha: a physician cant cure a bride, she only waits for the divine husband
physician and bride
The physician was called to the bride who would not eat, and he said no medicine could help, for she was only love-sick for her Bridegroom; write me a doha in which the soul is that waiting bride.
tilak and ocean, bride
doha with a tilak and the ocean about a bride soul awaiting her divine husband
The tilak is on her brow, the ocean before her; the bride waits for the Husband who comes from the infinite.
With the tilak glowing on her forehead the bride stands facing the ocean as if the Groom will come across its waves, and her heart is vast as the waters; compose a doha on the soul as a bride.
The bride put on her tilak and stood at the edge of the ocean all evening, as if the Groom might appear on the waves.
touchstone for the bride
The touchstone of patience tests the bride, and she passes, for her heart is the Groom's own.
The true bride is known by the touchstone of her patience, and the Groom accepts only the one who has waited without complaint; please write a doha in which the soul passes that test as a bride.
short doha about the soul as a bride passing the touchstone of the husband's test
My grandmother said a good wife is tested by waiting, as metal is tested on a touchstone, and she waited decades for her husband.
My little sister has been dressing up as a bride all week and says she is going to marry God when she grows up.

On the day of the wedding the bride rose early, bathed, and took her place at the head of the courtyard with the whole village singing, for the Bridegroom was about to arrive; write a long doha about this day.
doha: the soul as a bride awaiting the wedding day with her husband the divine
wedding day of the soul
The village sings, the bride is seated, and the Husband approaches; this is the day she was born for.
date palm, veiled bride
doha with a date palm and a veiled bride, the soul awaiting the divine groom
The date palm in our courtyard is where my cousin sat for her pre-wedding rituals, silent, as if already listening for her husband.
Under the date palm the bride sits veiled, and the Groom's hand lifts the cloth between her and the world.
Beneath the date palm, in the evening, the bride sat shy and silent, her face covered, waiting for the Groom to lift the veil, and I felt the soul was just like her; please compose a doha about it.
Tell me a story in a doha form in which the soul is a bride and the Lord is her bridegroom, and the long wait before the wedding is full of joy and anticipation rather than sorrow, please.
My niece is preparing for her wedding and she is not nervous at all, she says she is just so sure of him.
doha about the soul as bride, calm and happy that her husband the divine will come
The bride has no complaint against the wait, for the wedding is certain, and her Husband is faithful.
the happy bride-soul
hey a doha with a cloth sheet about the bride-soul awaiting her divine husband
My mother spread a fresh cloth sheet on my bridal bed the evening before my wedding, humming the song of the bride going to her Lord.
The cloth sheet is spread and the bridal bed is made; the bride waits, clean of all but the Groom's name.
cloth sheet for the groom

Please write a doha in which the cloth sheet spread over the bridal bed is the soul's offering, clean and unwrinkled, for the Bridegroom who will come to sit upon it and bless the bride with his presence.
A palanquin waits by the mosque for the bride, who will be carried to the Groom's village, and the soul is that bride leaving her father's place forever; please write a long doha.
doha: a palanquin outside the mosque and a bride leaving for her husband
The palanquin waits by the mosque, the bride rises, and the whole world blesses her going to the Husband.
palanquin, mosque, the bride
At the wedding a palanquin stood by the mosque, and the bride's brother carried her to it, weeping, as if she were going off to God.
At my wedding a heron stood by the pond and my uncle joked that I was the real philosopher's stone, changing my husband's life.
heron, philosopher's stone, bride
doha with a heron and a philosopher's stone about the bride soul's journey
The heron fakes devotion, the philosopher's stone lies unclaimed, and the bride walks past both to her true Husband.
The heron stood by the philosopher's stone beside the pond as the bride went by to meet her Groom, and neither could touch her pure intent; compose a doha in which the soul is that bride.
My grandmother always said the only fortunate woman is one whose husband is alive and healthy, and she touches her vermilion each morning.
I want to hear a doha where the soul is the happy wife of the Lord, lucky and blessed as the wife whose husband is alive and near, so she needs no ornament, no festival, and no other protector.
Blessed is the wife whose Husband lives; she needs no ornament and no other, for he alone is her treasure.
doha: soul as a blessed wife whose divine husband is ever-present
fortunate wife of the Lord
doha with milk and dew for a bride soul on her wedding morning
Milk in her cup and dew on the grass, the bride feels the Groom in every drop of the morning.
milk and dew, bride
On the wedding morning the bride drank warm milk and watched the dew shine on the grass, feeling that she was already a part of the Groom's world; compose a doha about the soul as a bride.
My sister drank her last glass of milk as an unmarried girl and stared at the dew on the lawn, saying it felt like the end of one world.
The river runs, the spinning wheel hums, and the bride weaves her own wedding dress for the Husband she has not yet seen.
My grandmother spun her own wedding cloth at the spinning wheel by the river, singing of a Groom she had never met.
river, spinning wheel, the bride
By the river the women are spinning at the spinning wheel their own wedding clothes, singing of the Groom to come; write a long doha in which the soul is a bride waiting for the Lord.
doha with a river and a spinning wheel for a bride-soul readying for the husband
The bride has covered her face with a veil and waits behind the screen, trembling with joy, because the Bridegroom is the Lord himself; please write a long doha about the soul as that bride.
please write a doha about the soul as a bride about to meet her divine groom
the veiled bride
Behind her veil the bride trembles with delight, for the Husband she was promised has come to the edge of the village.
My cousin's wedding is tomorrow and she keeps saying she is not afraid, just so happy that her husband is such a good man.
At my wedding the first dish was a bitter gourd, and my mother-in-law said that a good wife eats what her husband gives with love.
bitter gourd for the bride
doha: bitter gourd at a bride's feast, the soul accepting all from the divine husband
The bitter gourd on the wedding plate tastes sweet to the bride, for she takes it from the Husband's hand.
The bitter gourd on the wedding plate is for the bride to taste first, a custom that teaches the soul to accept both bitter and sweet from her Bridegroom's hand; write a doha, long and gentle.
doha about cotton and a bride soul preparing the wedding bed for her divine husband
I picked white cotton from the field to stuff the pillow of the bridal bed and, thinking of the Bridegroom, sang the whole day long; write a doha in which the soul is the bride preparing.
My mother picked cotton from our own field to make my wedding quilt and said it will keep you warm like your husband's love.
cotton for the wedding bed
Soft cotton for the bridal bed, and the bride sings; the Groom is certain and the day is near.
The lamp is lit on the wedding night and a bee circles the garland in the bride's hair, humming of the Bridegroom's arrival; please write a doha in which the soul is a bride awaiting her husband.
On my wedding night a lamp burned in the corner and a bee wandered in through the window, and my aunt said it was a blessing.
lamp, bee, the waiting bride
doha with a lamp and a bee for the bride soul waiting for her divine husband
Lamp lit, garland fresh, a bee hums the Groom's name to the bride who waits with open heart.
The yogi who has renounced the world told me that his true marriage is with the Lord, and he is the bride, and I found myself asking for a doha that says this; please write it for me.
The yogi leaves the world behind, and takes the Lord as husband; the ascetic is also the bride.
doha about a yogi who is really a bride of the Lord
There is a yogi near our village who wears bangles on one wrist and says he is the bride of Krishna, and nobody laughs anymore.
the yogi bride

The moneylender counted his coins beside the date palm while the bride walked on, uninterested in his wealth; she has no dowry but her devotion to the Groom. Compose a doha in which the soul is that bride.
doha: the bride soul ignores the moneylender and the date palm and goes to her divine husband
moneylender, date palm, bride
My cousin refused the moneylender's rich son under the date palm and said she would marry the man who sang with her to God.
The moneylender counts his coins by the date palm; the bride passes, richer by one Husband than all his wealth.
The bride gazes at the ocean and knows her Husband is that vastness, and she is the stream running to the shore.
bride and ocean
doha: the bride at the ocean, soul going to its divine husband
My cousin was married beside the ocean and said she felt as though her husband was the entire water waiting for her.
The bride stands at the edge of the ocean and imagines that her Groom is the whole vast water, waiting to receive her; write a long doha in which the soul is a bride going into her Lord.
Even in the busy market the bride buys nothing but bangles for her Bridegroom, who she knows will come at dusk; please write a long doha in which the soul is a bride in the world's bazaar.
bride in the market
My cousin spent the whole afternoon in the market buying bangles for her wedding and refused to buy anything else for herself.
The market is loud but the bride hears only the Groom's footstep; she buys nothing but the thought of his coming.
doha with a market and a bride soul waiting for the divine husband
please write a doha, the soul is a bride in red waiting for her divine husband
Dressed in red, the bride waits and the world waits with her, but only she knows that her Husband is already within her, ready to lead her into the real wedding; please write a doha.
When I wore my red wedding sari for the first time I felt like I was marrying something much larger than a man.
In red she sits, and the whole day glows; the Groom is in her breath, and the wedding is already begun.
bride in red
A moneylender demanded interest on my cousin's wedding loan and a thief stole her jewelry, yet she smiled and said her husband was all she needed.

The moneylender wanted the wedding jewels and a thief wanted the dowry, but the bride, thinking only of the Bridegroom, left them both with their petty fortunes; compose a doha in which the soul is the bride.
doha: moneylender and thief cannot touch the bride soul who waits for the divine groom
Moneylender and thief both grab at the dowry, but the bride has nothing and wants only her Husband.
moneylender, thief, bride
My niece didn't sleep at all before her wedding, she just lay there smiling at the ceiling saying he picked me.
The bride lies awake on her last maiden night, joyful, for the Lord has chosen her as His own.
chosen bride
I want a doha about the soul as a bride on the night before the wedding, when she lies awake with excitement rather than fear, because her Husband is the Lord who has chosen her above all others.
doha for the night before the soul's wedding to the divine groom
When the groom's family came to ask for her hand, the bride looked down and said yes, having said yes long ago in her heart; write a doha for the soul as a bride answering the Lord.
yes to the Groom
She said yes long before he asked; the bride was always the Groom's, as the soul was always the Lord's.
When they asked for my hand, I did not even need to think; my heart had answered before they finished their sentence.
a doha about the soul saying yes to the divine groom like a bride
Lamp lit and the lion on guard, the bride awaits her Groom, fearless and calm in the quiet room.
doha with a lamp and a lion for the bride soul awaiting her divine husband
lamp and lion, bride
At my cousin's wedding they lit a lamp at the doorway and my uncle held up a lion toy for luck, saying it would guard the bride.
A lamp burns at the entrance to the bridal chamber and a lion sits carved on the wall, guarding the bride who awaits the Bridegroom; compose a doha in which the soul is that waiting bride.
The palace was decorated for the wedding and the sand courtyard was swept clean, because the Bridegroom was a king, and the soul sat as the bride in the middle of it all; write me a doha.
doha with a palace and sand, soul as bride waiting for the divine king
My cousin's wedding was held in an old palace with fresh sand spread on the grounds, and she looked like a queen waiting for her king.
palace and sand, the bride
The palace is decorated, the sand swept; the bride is seated in waiting, the Husband is the king of kings.
doha with a crossroads and a bride, the soul waiting for her divine husband
My cousin stood at the crossroads at dusk in her wedding dress, watching for the groom's procession to come down the correct road.
bride at the crossroads
At the crossroads the bride watches all four roads, and knows that her Groom will come by the true one.
At the crossroads the bride waits for her Bridegroom's procession, hoping that he will take the right road to her, and I want a doha in which the soul is that bride watching all the roads.
The pot of water is on her head and the Groom in her heart; the bride walks lightly, for her wedding is near.
My sister carried a pot of water on her head to the pond at dawn on her wedding day, a custom that she said made her feel she was already his.
The bride carries a pot of water on her head and walks to the village pond, but her mind is only on the Groom who will arrive that evening; write a doha of the soul as bride.
doha with a pot of water for a bride soul awaiting the divine groom
pot of water, bride
My cousin sat on a stone outside the wedding hall for an hour because the groom's family was late, and she never once looked worried.
short doha for a bride sitting on a stone waiting for the divine groom
The bride sits on a stone and waits, patient as the earth, for the Husband whose promise has never failed.
the bride on a stone
A bride sits on a flat stone by the roadside, waiting with all the patience of the earth, for the Groom has promised he will come; please write a long doha in which the soul is that bride.
The washerman cleaned the wedding clothes at the pond while the potter shaped the last clay cup for the bride's chamber, and the bride waited calmly; compose a doha in which the soul is the bride.
washerman, potter, bride
The washerman cleans the cloth, the potter shapes the clay, and the bride is made ready to meet the Husband.
The village washerman and the potter were both busy for my sister's wedding, and she watched them quietly as though the whole village were making her ready.
doha with a washerman and a potter preparing the wedding of the bride soul
The priest recited verses at the wedding while the bride listened with her eyes closed, and she understood that the real vows are made not with a priest but silently with the Groom; write a doha.
At my wedding the priest droned on for hours, but the moment I really felt married was when I looked at my husband and we both smiled.
doha with a priest at the wedding of the soul and the divine
priest and bride
The priest recites the vows, the bride closes her eyes; the real marriage is made without a priest.
doha with a grindstone, the soul as a bride preparing for the divine groom
The grindstone turns, the grain turns to flour, and the bride sings, for the Groom's feast is hers to prepare.
The bride grinds the wheat on the grindstone before the wedding and sings, for the grain will make the feast for the Groom's arrival; please compose a long doha in which the soul is that bride.
My grandmother used to grind flour on the grindstone before every wedding in the village and sing songs about the bride meeting her Lord.
grindstone, the bride
The potter shapes the clay, the palace shines, and the bride sits waiting; all things are made ready for the Groom.
The potter shapes the clay and the palace is prepared for the wedding, and the bride, who is the soul, sits at the center, patient, while all things are made ready for the Lord; write a doha.
potter, palace, the bride
The potter delivered his clay pots to the palace where my cousin's wedding was held, and the bride sat in the middle of all that preparation.
doha with a potter and a palace for the soul as bride waiting for the divine husband
The furnace glows, the blind man sings, and the bride listens, for he sees the Husband the sighted cannot.
doha with a furnace and a blind man singing to the bride soul
furnace, blind man, bride

Beside the furnace where the wedding sweets are cooked a blind man sings of the Bridegroom, and the bride listens, because the blind man sees what others cannot; write a long doha for the soul as a bride.
A blind man sang at the wedding while the sweets cooked in the furnace, and the bride said he sang about her husband better than anyone.
When my aunt said the groom's party had arrived, I could not stand up, my knees had forgotten how.
I want a doha in which the soul as a bride is told by her sisters that her Groom has arrived and she is so overjoyed she cannot move from her seat, in the long hush before the rites begin.
doha about the bride soul frozen with joy when her divine groom arrives
the Groom has arrived
The sisters whisper that the Groom has come, and the bride sits as if turned to light, unable to rise.
